visual_evidence: A light-coloured flat wooden craft stick with a rounded end is held in the lower-centre of the frame.
A thin dark crack runs straight along the centreline of the stick parallel to its length and grain, starting at the rounded tip and extending toward the fingers.
The stick is slightly out of focus compared with the varnished wood table in the background.
The split remains closed so the internal fracture surface cannot be seen.
diagnosis.probable_cause: Cannot be determined from this photograph because the fracture surface is not exposed and the part is out of focus.
diagnosis.insufficient_reason: The wooden stick is slightly out of focus and the longitudinal split is closed, so the internal fracture surface is completely hidden from view. To diagnose the failure, separate the two halves (if fully fractured) or open the split slightly, tilt the fracture surface toward the camera, and take a sharp, close-up, well-lit photo focused directly on the exposed wood fibres.
